exploration.title: Chance Carnival
exploration.subject: Mathematics
exploration.summary: Compare observed results with expected chances.
exploration.question: Can fair chances give uneven results?
exploration.explanation: Expected chance comes from an outcome’s weight divided by total weight; observed share comes from one sample. Equal weights give equal chances, not equal counts. Larger samples usually settle nearer the expected shares, but a particular larger sample can be farther away. Each computer draw is independent, so past draws do not change the next one.

experiments.title: Compare sample sizes
experiments.instruction: With four equal weights, predict whether 10 counts must match. Run 10 trials, then extend the same sample to 1,000; change only sample size.
experiments.observe: Compare observed percentages with 25% expected for each outcome. Explain uneven counts and why one larger sample can still be farther from 25%.

experiments.title: Change one weight
experiments.instruction: Start with four weights of 1, then change outcome 1 to weight 4. Predict whether it is guaranteed next before running a fresh 1,000-trial sample.
experiments.observe: Compare outcome 1’s observed percentage with 57.1% expected. Explain why a higher chance is not a guaranteed next result.

exploration.misconception: Past draws do not make an outcome “due”; independent draws keep the same chances while weights stay fixed.
